item.title: Katsuo Tataki: Kochi's Seared Bonito — Guide
item.description: Katsuo no tataki is the definitive dish of Kochi, historically the province of Tosa, and one of Japan’s great regional specialities. A whole side of bonito is skewered and seared over a fierce blaze of burning rice straw, which chars and smokes the surface in seconds while leaving the inside raw and ruby-red. Sliced thick, it is served most famously ‘shio-tataki’ with just salt and garlic, or with tangy citrus ponzu, raw garlic, ginger and myoga.

item.title: Tosa Whale Cuisine in Kochi — Guide
item.description: Kochi, facing the Pacific, has a centuries-old connection to whales and whaling, and whale meat has a place in traditional Tosa cuisine. Historic whaling towns dotted the coast, and dishes using whale — as sashimi, simmered, or in the local ‘harihari’ hotpot with greens — were once a familiar part of the regional diet. Today whale is a niche traditional food served at a small number of specialist restaurants, presented as part of Kochi’s culinary heritage.
